detail: A framing question only. It asks for an order, which the section answers using c-plt-4 (simplified flag notes that the steps overlap).

Supported by g-hem-1 and c-plug-1. Calling it the 'first half' implies a sequence, but c-plug-1 carries a simplified flag whose fuller_truth covers the overlap, and m1-l08#3 says so explicitly. 'Quick' fits 'buys the body time'.
The four steps match c-plt-4. The clean sequence is covered by c-plt-4's simplified flag (the steps overlap in a real wound).
Megakaryocyte fragments, no nucleus, and a 7-10 day lifespan are all in c-plt-1 and c-plt-2. The aspirin forward reference adds no new fact.
A framing question. 'Touch the vessel wall all the time' is loose, but it matches sp-txa2 ('platelets circulate through vessels with intact endothelium... remain inactivated').
The single-layer lining is in g-endo-1 ('simple squamous epithelium'). The intact endothelium actively keeping platelets inactive is in c-endo-1.

Sentence 2 says 'Platelets also make a signal that pushes the other way, thromboxane A2.' The only cited claim, c-pgi2-1, says TXA2 pushes the other way but not that platelets make it, and none of its passages names the source of TXA2. Also, 'one of its tools' relies on c-endo-1's simplified flag (prostacyclin is one of several protections), but c-endo-1 is not cited here. Mechanistically the paragraph is correct.
correction: Add c-txa2-1 (an activated platelet makes TXA2) or c-cox-1 to claims, and add c-endo-1 for 'one of its tools'.

detail: Overstatement. 'It takes a break in the lining to start one' states that a break is necessary. c-endo-2 only says that a break exposes collagen and activating signals that trigger activation. Neither claim says a break is required, and clots can form without a physical break (for example, with a damaged but unbroken lining or slow flow). c-endo-1 is flagged simplified because the protections are more than one brake, which does not license an 'only a break' rule.
correction: "So platelets don't clot just anywhere. Normally, a break in the lining is what starts one."

detail: 'Fastest... before any plug exists' matches c-et-1 ('the first response to vessel injury is vascular spasm').
Smooth muscle contraction, narrowing, and limiting blood loss are all supported verbatim by c-et-1 (sp-platelet-activation, openstax-hemostasis).

Reflex neural signals and endothelin from damaged cells are in c-et-1. Serotonin maintaining vasoconstriction is in c-dg-2 ('maintains vasoconstriction'). TXA2 vasoconstriction is in c-txa2-2. 'Once platelets arrive... keep tight' is a fair ordering.
A framing question only.
Subendothelial collagen exposed by injury is in c-col-1 and g-sub-1. The 'wall is broken here' signal paraphrases 'one of the primary causes of clot formation'.

Sentences 1-2 (vWF binds collagen, platelets grab vWF via GPIb) are supported by c-vwf-1. Sentence 3, 'A receptor is a protein that grabs one specific molecule', overstates g-rec-1, which says 'selectively bind a specific molecule'. Receptors can bind more than one ligand, and this lesson itself later teaches that GPIIb/IIIa binds fibrinogen and vWF (c-gp2-1; c-fgn-1 adds fibrin, fibronectin, thrombospondin). As written, the definition contradicts m1-l07. It also drops the 'binding triggers a response' half of g-rec-1, which is the half that sets up GPIb triggering activation in m1-l05#1.
correction: "A receptor is a protein on the cell that selectively grabs a particular molecule, and that grip sends a signal into the cell."

detail: Storage in endothelial Weibel-Palade bodies and platelet alpha granules, ready for release, is in c-vwf-2. Note that platelet vWF is released only after activation (c-gpib-1 passage), which the lesson covers in the next section. Not an error.

'Remember the chain: collagen, then vWF, then GPIb' teaches a single adhesion route. The cited claim, c-vwf-1, has no simplified flag. Platelets also bind collagen directly through GPVI and use GPIIb/IIIa for firm adhesion. This is true but incomplete and is acceptable only with a flag, which exists on c-gpib-1 (fuller_truth names GPVI and GPIIb/IIIa).
correction: Add c-gpib-1 to claims so the simplified flag travels with this mnemonic. Optionally: "the first grip goes collagen, then vWF, then GPIb."

detail: A framing question. Implying 'next' is fine because c-gpib-1 says GPIb-vWF binding triggers activation.

GPIb-vWF helping activate the platelet is in c-gpib-1 (simplified flag: not the only trigger). Collagen and signals from other platelets are in c-endo-2. Leaving out thrombin is incompleteness covered by c-gpib-1's fuller_truth.

Disc to sphere is in sp-txa2, 'spiked' is in openstax-hemostasis, and 'much better at sticking' matches 'greatly facilitates the adhesion of platelets to each other and components of the extracellular matrix' (c-plt-3).

Content is supported: degranulation (g-act-1), dense granules holding ADP, serotonin, and calcium (c-dg-1), and alpha granules holding proteins including vWF and fibrinogen (c-ag-1). 'Empties its granules' slightly overstates 'release of hemostatic mediators from the platelet's granules', since release need not be complete.
correction: "It also releases the contents of its granules, small storage packets inside it."

detail: A framing question only.
ADP and TXA2 as activating signals in a positive feedback loop are supported by c-plt-5 and c-txa2-1 (sp-txa2 'positive-feedback mediator'; sp-platelet-activation 'positive feedback loop').
ADP from dense granules binding P2Y12, which turns on GPIIb/IIIa, is in c-adp-1 and c-p2y12-1. Naming P2Y12 alone is covered by c-adp-1's simplified flag (P2Y1 also).

Sentence 1, 'Thromboxane A2 isn't stored', is not stated by c-cox-1 or c-txa2-1 or their passages. They say the activated platelet makes or produces it, not that it is never stored. The fact is physiologically true (it is made on demand), but it is a new statement. Sentence 2 (made by COX-1, constitutively present) is supported by c-cox-1, and the one-step simplification is flagged.
correction: Reword to what the claims support: "Unlike ADP, thromboxane A2 is made on the spot by the activated platelet, using an enzyme called COX-1, which is always present in platelets." Or add a claim and passage stating that TXA2 is synthesized rather than stored.

detail: Aspirin blocking COX-1 (c-asa-1) and clopidogrel, prasugrel, and ticagrelor blocking P2Y12 (c-clop-1, c-pras-1, c-tica-1) are all supported, with brand names in pmc-p2y12-review.
A framing question only.
Inactive on a resting platelet and gripping only after activation is in c-gp2-1 ('requires prior activation of the integrin'; inside-out signaling).

One fibrinogen linking GPIIb/IIIa on two platelets is in c-fgn-1 ('acts as a link between GPIIb/IIIa receptors on different platelets'). Leaving out vWF as a second bridge is minor, and the cited c-gp2-1 names it. Optional addition: '(vWF can bridge too)'.

This teaches the two receptors as strictly separate ('GPIb is for sticking to the wound... GPIIb/IIIa is for sticking to each other'). Yet the cited c-gp2-2 passage itself says GPIIb/IIIa engagement 'is involved in platelet firm adhesion to the subendothelium', so GPIIb/IIIa also helps hold platelets to the wound. Neither c-gp2-2 nor g-adag-1 carries a simplified flag. The order (GPIb first, GPIIb/IIIa after) is supported. The strict division of roles needs a flag or a softer wording.
correction: Add c-gpib-1 (its fuller_truth names GPIIb/IIIa among the adhesion receptors), or reword: "GPIb gives the first grip on the wound (adhesion). GPIIb/IIIa comes second and mainly links platelets to each other (aggregation), though it also firms up their hold on the wound."

detail: A framing question only.
'Temporarily seal a small opening... buys the body time' (c-plug-1).

Coagulation reinforcing the plug with fibrin is in c-plug-1 and g-hem-1. Fibrin as an insoluble filament derived from fibrinogen whose mesh traps platelets and blood cells is in g-fib-1. 'Tough' fits 'robust'. No intrinsic/extrinsic framing is used.

Supported by c-plug-1's simplified.fuller_truth and its sources (pmc-vitk-cycle, sp-clotting-factors) and by g-ca-1. This is the paragraph that correctly undoes the sequence implied in m1-l01, consistent with the cell-based model. Minor nuance: pmc-vitk-cycle says damaged endothelial cells also serve as a surface, so 'the surface' is slightly exclusive, but it matches the reviewed fuller_truth wording.
A framing question only.

The signs are supported by c-plug-2, g-pet-1, and g-muc-1. 'Signature' with no hedge overstates c-plug-2's 'typically'. The cited sp-petechiae passage lists coagulation disorders and loss of vascular integrity as causes of petechiae and purpura too, so these signs suggest but do not prove a platelet problem.
correction: "Platelet problems typically show up as bleeding into the skin and the moist linings of the body..."

detail: The 150,000/uL threshold for thrombocytopenia is in c-pc-1. Mild drops being asymptomatic and spontaneous bleeding under about 10,000-20,000 is in c-pc-2 (sp-thrombocytopenia under 20,000; sp-histology under 10x10^9/L).

The facts are supported (c-vwd-1, simplified flag for the vWD types; c-pc-3). But the lead phrase 'Enough platelets that can't grip' suggests the platelets themselves are defective. The cited sp-platelet-activation passage says vWD is 'not a platelet disorder': the platelets are normal and lack the vWF anchor. 'A normal count doesn't prove platelets work' is likewise better framed as 'doesn't prove the plug can form'.
correction: "Enough platelets, but nothing to grip: ... The platelet count is typically normal, but adhesion is weak, so a normal count doesn't prove the plug can form."

detail: Bernard-Soulier (GPIb deficiency, impaired adhesion) is in c-gpib-2. Glanzmann (GPIIb/IIIa deficiency, impaired aggregation) is in c-gp2-3.
A framing question. The drug and brand names are supported in the section.
Irreversible COX-1 block, no TXA2, and reduced aggregation are in c-asa-1.

Sentences 1-2 are supported by c-cox-2 (simplified flag) and c-asa-2. Sentence 3, '...not how long the drug stays in the blood', adds a pharmacokinetic contrast that neither cited claim states. The 'new platelet production rather than pharmacokinetics' wording exists only in dm-effient, for prasugrel, under c-pras-1, which is not cited here. The point is true, but it is new for aspirin.
correction: Either drop the last clause ("It's the platelet's lifespan that counts.") or cite a source passage on aspirin's short plasma persistence versus its lasting effect.

detail: Irreversible P2Y12 block leading to no GPIIb/IIIa activation is in c-clop-1. Both being prodrugs is in c-clop-2 and c-pras-1. Recovery within about 5 days for clopidogrel (c-clop-3) and 5-9 days for prasugrel with new platelet production (c-pras-1) is supported. Suggestion only: add c-p2y12-1 so the GPIIb/IIIa consequence is explicitly cited for prasugrel as well.
Reversible P2Y12 block, 'reversible does not mean short', and IPA similar to placebo at 5 days are all in c-tica-1 (dm-brilinta).
